page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server instance featuring 12 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes hyperthreading, a 16 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX and AES instructions. System memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a local 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The server is equipped with two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM with 16 GB per GPU. In benchmark evaluations, the hardware demonstrates strong capabilities in parallel processing and machine learning workloads. LLM inference testing shows top-tier prompt processing speeds, reaching 8665.1 tokens per second with a small 135M model and 613.27 tokens per second with a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are also competitive, achieving 32.35 tokens per second on the 7B model. General compute benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core at 8523.0 and Passmark CPU at 20085.48, align with average performance tiers for this hardware class.

This instance offers a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive and GPU-accelerated tasks, providing high memory density and dedicated CPU resources without the premium cost of top-tier enterprise compute chips. However, single-core performance is moderate, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1289.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1754.67. Consequently, it is best suited for workloads that can leverage multi-threading and GPU acceleration, such as medium-scale LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations, rather than single-threaded CPU-bound applications.
description: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server instance designed for memory-intensive and parallel computing workloads. It features 12 vCPUs on a 6-core Intel x86_64 architecture running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory and a 700 GB NVMe SSD. Graphics and acceleration are driven by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs with a total of 32 GB VRAM. Benchmarks highlight top-tier prompt processing performance for large language models, reaching 613.27 tokens per second on a 7B model, alongside solid multi-core processing capabilities. While single-core performance is moderate, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dual-GPU configuration make this instance highly cost-efficient for multi-threaded applications. It is well-suited for medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations.
